summary: Scope reviewed: behavioral-spec.md 'Mode-B in-loop publish (Sprint 4)' section (REQ-23/24/25, lines 105-126) and verification-architecture.md PROP-24/25/26 (lines 42-44) + renumbered Sprint 4-8 plan (lines 78-84). This change wires the previously human/main-agent-triggered real publish click (REQ-21) into run.sh's unattended Mode-B branch via a newly-introduced SHARED, importable core function. Six concrete gaps found. (1) REQ-23/PROP-24's claim that Mode A is 'structurally unable to reach' the shared publish-click function relies on a grep target ('unchanged from Sprint 1-2') that checked absence of the click string in Mode-A's OWN, previously click-free script files -- it does not cover the NEW risk surface introduced by this very sprint: run.sh itself now imports/calls the shared click function from its Mode-B branch, so a branch-selection bug in run.sh could reach it under AUTONOMY=off without touching the old grep target at all. No dynamic call-count wiring test (of the kind PROP-6 already established for the analogous Mode-A-never-calls-publish invariant) is required for this new call site. (2) 'The logic SHALL NOT be duplicated/reinvented' (REQ-23) is operationalized only as 'grep: no duplicated/reinvented logic' (PROP-24), which is not a well-defined, mechanically executable oracle, and the spec never defines the shared function's boundary -- whether the try/except/finally exception-safety and pre-publish confirmation are INSIDE the shared unit (safe) or left to be re-wrapped by each caller (silent-divergence risk, the exact FIND-004-regression risk the review context called out). (3) REQ-24 is asymmetric: it specifies the failure/UNCONFIRMED path in detail but never restates REQ-22's success-path recording requirement (URL+timestamp+result for V4 tracking) for the in-loop case, and no PROP tests the success-recording path at all -- an always-UNCONFIRMED stub implementation would pass every listed test while silently breaking V4 earn tracking. (4) PROP-26's grep oracle ('no hardcoded AUTONOMY=on default in source') does not clearly extend to install-time config templates/scaffolding; a config file shipped with AUTONOMY pre-set to on (or a ratio pre-set to always-Mode-B) would pass the literal grep while being functionally identical to a hardcoded default -- the exact loophole this review was asked to probe. (5) REQ-23's binary AUTONOMY=on/off gate and REQ-25's per-wake ratio/mix model are never explicitly reconciled -- nothing states that REQ-23 gates on the ratio-DERIVED effective per-wake mode, leaving room for the ratio config to be stored but never actually consulted. (6) PROP-26 (the graduation/ratio safety governor, REQ-25) is marked NOT required for convergence while PROP-24/25 (the publish mechanics it is meant to throttle) are required -- inconsistent given the irreversible, monetized, publicly-visible nature of the action being gated. None of these are satisfied by the current wording; all are concrete, citable, and blocking for a strict-mode financial/safety sprint contract.
